about: Every command of the Discord and Slack apps and the web shortcuts. scripts/sync-pages.js renders the cards on /commands, /discord and /slack from this file; test/parity.test.js checks the names against discord/src/commands.js and slack/src/game.js.

discord.label: Discord
discord.intro: Add Who's Bluffing to your apps, then type `/bluff party` in a chat to start a Memes round with friends. Replies marked “only you” are private. Server-only commands need the app added to that server.

commands.name: /bluff party
commands.does: Starts a shared Memes round. Friends tap Join to play the same ten questions privately. Joining shares your Discord display name and finished score in this chat. Tap Results to refresh completed scores; after you finish, Rematch starts a new shared round. Each round expires after one hour. Public posts follow the chat’s app permissions.

commands.name: /bluff play
commands.does: A private 10-question round (only you): pick A or B, say how sure you are, see the answer and your points, then Next. It ends with your score, your type and a Challenge button that posts your challenge link in the channel.

commands.name: /bluff question
commands.does: Posts today’s question in this channel now. If today’s question is already up, it links to it instead.
commands.who: Anyone in a server with the app installed

commands.name: /bluff stats
commands.does: Posts this server’s leaderboard for the last 30 days in the channel: the top 10 by points and how many members answered.
commands.who: Anyone in a server with the app installed

commands.name: /bluff setup
commands.does: Sets where and when the daily question goes, how many hours later the answer is revealed, and roast mode. Every option is optional: a missing one keeps its value. A new channel gets a short hello, which also checks that Who's Bluffing may post there.

options.name: channel
options.does: where the daily question goes (a text or announcement channel)

options.name: hour
options.does: the posting hour in UTC, 0 to 23 (default 14); members see the post and reveal times in their own time zone

options.name: reveal
options.does: hours from the post to the reveal, 2 to 23 (new servers start at 20)

options.name: roast
options.does: on or off (default off): on names the biggest bluffer in the reveal

commands.name: /bluff reveal
commands.does: Reveals today’s answer now instead of waiting for the scheduled reveal.

commands.name: /bluff help
commands.does: How Who's Bluffing works and the command list (only you).

commands.name: /bluff invite
commands.does: Links to add Who's Bluffing to your apps or to a server (only you).

trouble.a: Use [Add to my apps](/discord) for your own commands, or have an admin use Add to server for everyone there. Then reload Discord (Ctrl+R or Cmd+R). The server or channel may also restrict app commands.

trouble.q: My friends can’t see the round
trouble.a: A server can prevent personal apps from posting publicly with the Use External Apps permission. Who's Bluffing respects that setting. Ask an admin whether games are welcome there, or start `/bluff party` in a group chat where everyone wants to play.

trouble.q: “Only members with the Manage Server permission can do that”
trouble.a: `/bluff setup` and `/bluff reveal` need the Manage Server or Administrator permission. Ask someone who has it, or have an admin give your role Manage Server.

trouble.q: The server leaderboard says “a member” instead of names
trouble.a: The `/bluff stats` leaderboard looks up server members. If everyone shows as “a member”, please [tell us on GitHub](https://github.com/rongtnt/whos-bluffing/issues). Only the first 1,000 members of a server can be named. Friend rounds use the display name you share when joining instead.

Update your Discord app (or reload the browser tab) and try again: older versions can’t show the buttons. If it keeps happening, the game server may be down for a moment; the [status page](/status) shows whether it answers.
Give Who's Bluffing the View Channel and Send Messages permissions in that channel, or pick another one with `/bluff setup channel:`.
That is normal. Who's Bluffing answers through Discord’s interactions endpoint and never connects to the live gateway, so it always looks offline while it works.

slack.label: Slack
slack.intro: Type them in any channel. Anything else after `/bluff` shows the command list, only to you.

commands.name: /bluff
commands.does: Posts today’s question in this channel. In the chosen channel (or when none is chosen yet) it becomes the day’s post; elsewhere it posts a copy whose answers count the same. After today’s reveal it posts nothing and says so.

commands.name: /bluff setup #channel [hour] [roast on|off] [reveal N]
commands.does: Posts the question in #channel every day at that hour in your time zone, and reveals the answer N hours later. Type # and pick the channel so Slack links it. Everyone sees the times in their own time zone.

options.name: #channel
options.does: where the daily question goes; for a private channel, run `/invite @whosbluffing` in it first

options.name: hour
options.does: 0 to 23 in your Slack time zone; add `utc` after it for UTC (left out: 14:00 UTC)

options.name: roast on|off
options.does: on names the biggest bluffer at the reveal and shows negative points (off by default)

options.name: reveal N
options.does: hours from the post to the reveal, 2 to 23 (default 8)

commands.name: /bluff setup roast on|off
commands.does: Changes roast mode only; the channel and the hour stay as they are. `/bluff setup reveal N` changes only the hours to the reveal.

commands.name: /bluff reveal
commands.does: Reveals the open question now, for everyone.

commands.name: /bluff stats
commands.does: Posts this workspace’s leaderboard for the last 30 days in the channel: the top 10 by total points (ties: more answers first) and how many members answered. Only revealed days count.

trouble.q: Slack says `/bluff` is not a valid command
trouble.a: Who's Bluffing isn’t installed in this workspace, or was removed. Install it again from the [Add to Slack](/slack) link.
The channel is private. Run `/invite @whosbluffing` in it, then `/bluff setup #channel` again. Public channels work without an invite.

The hour you type is read in your Slack time zone (or in UTC with `utc` after it) and kept in UTC; the setup reply shows both. Who's Bluffing checks at the top of every hour and posts once a day, as soon as your hour has come; if you set it up after that hour, today’s question posts at the next full hour. Run `/bluff setup #channel HH` to check the channel and hour.
The private picker uses a Slack link that lasts 30 minutes after you tap A or B. Tap A or B again.
The game server didn’t answer. Try again in a minute; the [status page](/status) shows whether it is up.

web.label: Web shortcuts
web.intro: Keys work while a question or its answer is on screen; addresses work in any browser.

commands.name: A or B
commands.does: Picks answer A or B.
commands.who: Anyone, while a question is on screen

commands.does: Says how sure you are once you have picked an answer: 5 for 50%, 6 for 60% and so on, 0 for 100%.
commands.who: Anyone, while a question is on screen

commands.name: N or Enter
commands.does: Goes to the next question, or to your score after the last one.
commands.who: Anyone, while an answer is on screen

commands.name: whosbluffing.com
commands.does: Choose a topic and difficulty, then play as many ten-question rounds as you like.

commands.name: whosbluffing.com/?pack=history&difficulty=brutal
commands.does: Opens the home page with that pack and difficulty picked for your quick rounds.

options.name: pack
options.does: `all`, or a pack such as `geography`, `history` or `countries`

commands.name: whosbluffing.com/c/…
commands.does: A challenge link from “Challenge a friend”: plays the same ten questions, then shows both scores side by side.

commands.name: whosbluffing.com/test
commands.does: The 5-minute full assessment: twelve two-choice questions with a confidence each and six 90% ranges.

options.name: c
options.does: a class code: `/test?c=CODE` joins that class

commands.name: whosbluffing.com/class
commands.does: Creates a class code and a live dashboard of the class’s answers (aggregates only, from 5 students).

commands.name: whosbluffing.com/stats
commands.does: The total number of anonymous players who have played.

trouble.a: It needs JavaScript. Reload the page; if an extension blocks scripts, allow this site.
Click the page first so it has the focus, and make sure the cursor isn’t in a text box. Keys work only while a question or its answer is on screen.

trouble.q: My streak or my round in progress disappeared
trouble.a: Both live in your browser’s storage. A private window or clearing the site’s data starts fresh.
Your answer is still on screen: press Try again. If it keeps happening, the [status page](/status) shows whether the game server answers.
